steps.label: Cortical nephrons
steps.why: A short loop that hardly enters the medulla cannot build a strong salt gradient, so these nephrons do little concentrating.
common_mistakes: Giving cortical nephrons a long loop. Their loop is short.
Writing that they have vasa recta. They lack it.
steps.memory_tip: Cortical: high up, short loop, no vasa recta.
steps.margin_note: Two points each, written as a comparison.

steps.label: Juxtamedullary nephrons
steps.why: The long loop and its vasa recta together build the salt gradient that lets the kidney make concentrated urine.
common_mistakes: Placing them in the cortex. They lie near the medulla.
Leaving out the vasa recta, which is the marked difference.
steps.memory_tip: Juxtamedullary: near the medulla, long loop, vasa recta present.
steps.margin_note: Finish with the vasa recta. It is the key difference.
